correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, the maximality lemma follows directly from all cross-part edges and no within-part edges. The sorted-prefix pairing supplies exactly n nonempty independent sets of sizes 1 or 2. All full bipartite EF1 allocations are counted by choosing part-assigned agent sets and balance-size choices; nonfull allocations require all n agents to be nonempty and one part to be exhaustively allocated, yielding D_n. The odd symmetric family has no full balanced allocation by parity and exactly 2t! one-sided fair outcomes. Nonfair full outcomes are enumerated by disjoint sets of i,j active agents and Stirling surjections. The explicit partition subfamilies prove the stated probability decay. 121 exact count comparisons, 116020 constructive cases, and independent K_{3,3} outcome enumeration passed; no finite experiment substitutes for the analytic argument.

value.rationale: Recent maximal-EF1 research explicitly motivates control of wastage. Constructive existence for all complete multipartite graphs, an exact symbolic count across all complete bipartite parameter triples, and a sharp infinite family losing half the goods constitute a motivated structural classification. Superexponential rarity under an explicit uniform maximal-allocation benchmark adds quantitative value. The result does not rely on an arbitrary finite slice or a known-table recalculation.
